EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Rotating Machinery is used in your life every single day.
INTRODUCTIONM
From a simple fan to your car's alternator, rotating machinery is used frequently.
Because of their frequent use, a technician must understand rotating machinery.
To understand rotating machines, a technician must understand the theory of magnetism and electromagnetics.
Let's begin the lesson on INTRODUCTION TO ROTATING MACHINERY................
LESSON MENU
INTRODUCTION TO ROTATING MACHINERY
In this lesson you will learn about Rotating Machinery.....
DISCUSSION
Rotating machines are composed of a wide variety of devices.
Any device which exhibits a rotating shaft is called a rotating machine.
Rotating machines are commonly called motors.
Actually, rotating machines are more than motors alone.....
A generator is also classified as a rotating machine.
A motor is a device that produces a mechanical force or work from an electrical input.
A fan is one example of a motor............................
A fan runs on electricity from either a wall outlet or a battery source.
The fans motor takes the electric input and causes a mechanical output.
The output from the motor is the turning of fan blades producing forced air flow.
A generator is a device that produces an electrical output from a mechanical input.
A generator could get it's input from an engine, a nuclear reactor or some other device.
This mechanical input causes the generator to produce or generate an electrical output.
The electrical energy then can be used as an input to a motor. For example, the power company uses a generator, you use the electricity to run a fan.
Motors are classified as either Incremental or Continuous..

MAGNETISM AND ELECTROMAGNETISM
Magnetism is a force that attracts or repels certain types of metal objects. It is what makes rotating machinery operate.
DISCUSSION
To understand magnetism you need to look at the characteristics of a magnet.
Each end of a magnet has a pole. One end is the north pole and the other end is the south pole.
All magnets have lines of force called flux lines.
The flux lines leave the north pole and enter the south pole of the magnet.
The flux lines form a magnetic field around the magnet.
The flux lines form a magnetic field around the magnet.....
DEFINITION
The more flux lines a magnet has, the stronger the magnetic field.
The stronger the magnetic field (more flux lines), the more work or attraction the magnet can perform.
Magnets follow two simple rules:...........................
TDX OPERATIONAL CHECK
If the north and south poles of two magnets are brought together, a magnetic attraction occurs.
The flux lines of each magnet combine causing the magnets to come together and become one magnet.
If like poles of two magnets are brought together, they will repel each other.
The repelling force is as strong as the force of attraction when unlike poles are brought together.
Rotating machinery uses attraction or repulsion to change electrical energy to mechanical energy and mechanical energy to electrical energy.
TDX OPERATIONAL CHECK
However, instead of using a natural magnet, man made magnets are used.
Rotating machinery normally uses electromagnets. Electromagnets are man made.
Electromagnets are made by applying electricity to magnetic materials.
When electric current passes through a conductor, a small circular magnetic field, called magnemotive force (MMF), is generated.
MMF is the magnetic field of the conductor induced by the flow of current.
It is the MMF that produces a motor. Let's see.
In a generator, mechanical energy is changed to electrical energy.
When a conductor is moved through a magnetic field, a current is produced in the conductor by induced EMF.
The right hand rule still applies. But, this time the direction of current flow is determined.
Note that this is opposite of passing current through a conductor.
The right hand rule still applies. But, this time the direction of current flow is determined.

RIGHT HAND RULE - Place the center finger of your right hand in the direction of current flow through the conductor. Place your first finger in the direction of the magnetic field. Your thumb will point in the direction that the conductor will rotate.
The current carrying conductor, when placed in a magnetic field, produces its own electromagnetic field (EMF).
The direction of the field can be determined using the left hand rule..
The direction of the field can be determined using the left hand rule..
DEFINITION
Since current is flowing into the conductor (represented by an X), the induced electromagnetic field is traveling in a CCW direction.
The induced electromagnetic field and the magnetic field interact.
These two interacting forces cause the conductor to go into motion.
The direction of motion that the conductor follows can be determined by the right hand rule.

RIGHT HAND RULE - Place the center finger of your right hand in the direction of current flow through the conductor. Place your first finger in the direction of the magnetic field. Your thumb will point in the direction that the conductor will rotate.
DEFINITION
The moving conductor is a normal phenomenon in magnetic theory. This is motor action.
Examine the field interactions carefully...................
At the top interaction point the electromagnetic and magnetic fields are in opposite directions.
Remember opposite fields attract. This tends to pull the conductor upward.
At the bottom interaction point, the two fields are in the same direction.
Remember, like fields repel. This tends to push the conductor upward.
As you can see, the conductor will be forced up and out of the field.
These combined actions illustrate why the conductor moves in the magnetic field.
You will see how this motion is changed to the rotating motion of a motor later.
The principles of magnetism are also used in generators....
All rotating machinery work under the fundamental principles of magnetism and electromagnetism.
